Community reports focus on latency of minutes for standard queries (undermind-comm-14/15/16), not on a notify-on-completion workflow for the deep MCP research tool. Missing for 10: explicit documentation linking job completion to a notification/alert, and independent confirmation of true unattended multi-hour runs with completion alerts.

Undermind explicitly offers alert-style notification ('Get notified whenever relevant papers are published') and paper starring/curation for ongoing monitoring, directly matching the standing-search/alert use case. However, evidence is a single first-party mention with no detail on alert configuration, frequency, delivery channel, or independent user corroboration of this specific feature. Missing for 10: detailed docs on alert setup/customization, independent/community confirmation the alerting feature works as described, and info on how alerts integrate with saved searches vs. folders.

Undermind exposes a first-party MCP server with tools mirroring key UI capabilities (deep literature review, full-text PDF Q&A, note creation, folder curation, starring) and separately advertises a 'Programmatic queries via API' feature for enterprise customers, showing real intent toward API-level parity. However, probes found no public OpenAPI spec, docs, or llms.txt (404s), and the enterprise API is not documented enough to confirm it covers the full UI surface (e.g., alerts/notifications, workspace management). Missing for 10: publicly documented/openapi-verifiable API, evidence of full feature parity beyond MCP tools, and independent confirmation the enterprise API actually mirrors all UI functions.

No evidence of any data export feature or open-format export capability; Undermind's docs describe MCP integration, search, and workspace features but nothing about exporting user data or leaving with it in an open format. Probe results confirm no docs/openapi endpoints exist that might hint at export functionality.

Undermind is a closed, proprietary SaaS research/search product; there is no evidence of any open-source license or public source repository, and this is a commercial hosted service, not an open-source project, so the open-source-license axis doesn't apply.

Undermind is a hosted SaaS research/search service (accessed via MCP server, web app, or API); there is no evidence it is an open-source or self-hostable core product, and self-hosting is not a plausible axis for this kind of proprietary cloud research engine.

Undermind's docs describe reading and analyzing full-text PDFs it discovers via search, curating them into folders, and creating notes/synthesis — but there is no evidence of a user-upload feature for arbitrary personal PDFs or an external corpus for the agent to research over. Community and docs evidence focuses entirely on Undermind's own search/discovery pipeline, not ingestion of user-supplied documents.
No evidence anywhere in the pack about data residency, region selection, or storage location controls for Undermind; all evidence concerns literature search features and MCP integration.
No evidence in the pack addresses data-training opt-out, privacy policy commitments, or any statement about how user queries/documents are or aren't used to train AI models.

No evidence anywhere in the pack about data retention policies, deletion controls, or privacy settings for user data/queries/documents; the documentation focuses only on search/MCP/research features. Missing for 10: any mention of data retention settings, account/data deletion mechanism, or privacy policy controls.
No evidence in the pack mentions telemetry, usage tracking, opt-out settings, or privacy controls for Undermind; the docs focus on research/search features and MCP integration.

Undermind is explicitly a scholarly/literature research engine that reads full-text PDFs, follows citations and key authors, and traces statements back to source papers, and community feedback confirms it surfaces relevant academic papers beyond simple web search (comparisons to Google Scholar, Arxiv, Science Direct). Some users note gaps like missing gray literature/dissertations, indicating imperfect but genuine coverage of scholarly sources. Missing for 10: independent benchmarking against dedicated scholarly databases (PubMed, Web of Science) and no clear evidence of primary-source archival material beyond papers.

Evidence shows workspaces, files, and folders staying available across sessions and to agents, but there is no mention of sharing a session/report with collaborators, multi-user permissions, view/edit links, or team collaboration features. Missing for 10: any documentation of session/report sharing, collaborator invites, or permissioned access.

Docs describe an autonomous review that 'stops only when new searches stop finding relevant papers,' implying the depth/exhaustiveness is self-determined by the system rather than user-configurable, and no evidence shows settings for scope, effort, or in-flight adjustment of a run. Community feedback even flags the 'Discovery Progress and Exhaustiveness' indicator as confusing rather than as a steerable control.

Undermind produces a ranked list of papers with a written synthesis and can create/edit Markdown notes, syntheses, and reports with citations linking back to sources, which supports shareable structured output. However, there is no evidence of built-in tables, formal 'sections' structuring, or a dedicated stakeholder-facing report/export format beyond Markdown notes. Missing for 10: explicit table generation, multi-section report templates, and export/sharing formats (PDF/Word) for stakeholders beyond in-workspace Markdown.

Undermind's MCP tools support open-ended literature review with ranked results, full-text PDF question-answering across many papers, and note/synthesis creation, which covers much of a screening-and-extraction workflow (undermind-docs-4, undermind-docs-5, undermind-docs-6, undermind-docs-7). However, there is no evidence of formal criteria-based screening (e.g., inclusion/exclusion rules) or structured, consistent extraction fields across a batch of papers, and community feedback notes gaps in coverage (missed gray literature/theses) that could undermine consistency (undermind-comm-1, undermind-comm-4). Missing for 10: explicit support for defined screening criteria, structured/consistent extraction schema, and independent validation of consistency at scale.

Evidence only hints at tiering ('10x higher usage limits', unlimited workspaces on some plan) but provides no actual pricing page, tier names, cost figures, or specific usage caps a researcher could evaluate before committing; community comments even ask for pay-per-query options, suggesting the current pricing model isn't clearly documented.
